title: Bearing Wear Guide
text: Bearing Wear Guide (MNT-001) - Symptoms and Signals: Bearing wear shows as a steady rise in vibration, usually over 5 to 12 days, followed by a smaller rise in temperature and motor current. Vibration climbs slowly at first and then quickly in the last days before failure. Audible grinding or whining noise is common.

title: Bearing Wear Guide
text: Bearing Wear Guide (MNT-001) - Alert Thresholds: Limits are set per asset from its baseline: ALERT when vibration is at least 2.2x baseline, temperature is at least baseline + 15 C, or motor current is at least 1.25x baseline. ALARM when vibration is at least 3.0x baseline or temperature is at least baseline + 25 C. For bearing wear, vibration is the earliest and most reliable signal.

title: Bearing Wear Guide
text: Bearing Wear Guide (MNT-001) - Likely Causes: Insufficient or contaminated grease, shaft misalignment, overload, normal end of life, or poor installation. Check the lubrication history before blaming the bearing alone.

title: Bearing Wear Guide
text: Bearing Wear Guide (MNT-001) - Recommended Actions: On ALERT, raise an inspection work order within the SOP-001 time limit and re-check vibration every shift. On ALARM, plan a bearing replacement at the next stop. Replace the bearing, re-grease, check alignment, and record vibration after restart.

title: Bearing Wear Guide
text: Bearing Wear Guide (MNT-001) - Parts and Downtime: Typical repair takes 24 to 48 hours. Parts: deep groove bearing or spindle bearing set, grease cartridge. Confirm stock at the plant before scheduling.

title: Imbalance and Misalignment Guide
text: Imbalance and Misalignment Guide (MNT-002) - Symptoms and Signals: Imbalance and misalignment raise vibration and make the rotation speed (RPM) less steady. Temperature rises only slightly. Motor current rises a little.

title: Imbalance and Misalignment Guide
text: Imbalance and Misalignment Guide (MNT-002) - Alert Thresholds: Limits are set per asset from its baseline: ALERT when vibration is at least 2.2x baseline, temperature is at least baseline + 15 C, or motor current is at least 1.25x baseline. ALARM when vibration is at least 3.0x baseline or temperature is at least baseline + 25 C. An unusually jittery RPM reading together with rising vibration points to this fault.

title: Imbalance and Misalignment Guide
text: Imbalance and Misalignment Guide (MNT-002) - Likely Causes: Loose coupling or foundation bolts, worn coupling element, uneven material build-up on the rotor, or a recent re-installation.

title: Imbalance and Misalignment Guide
text: Imbalance and Misalignment Guide (MNT-002) - Recommended Actions: Inspect coupling and bolts, re-align the shaft with a dial gauge or laser tool, and balance the rotor if needed. Confirm vibration after restart is back near baseline.

title: Imbalance and Misalignment Guide
text: Imbalance and Misalignment Guide (MNT-002) - Parts and Downtime: Typical repair takes 8 to 16 hours. Parts: flexible coupling element, balancing weight kit.

title: Overheating and Cooling Fault Guide
text: Overheating and Cooling Fault Guide (MNT-003) - Symptoms and Signals: Overheating shows as a rapid temperature rise over several days, with a modest rise in motor current. Vibration changes very little, which separates this fault from bearing wear.

title: Overheating and Cooling Fault Guide
text: Overheating and Cooling Fault Guide (MNT-003) - Alert Thresholds: Limits are set per asset from its baseline: ALERT when vibration is at least 2.2x baseline, temperature is at least baseline + 15 C, or motor current is at least 1.25x baseline. ALARM when vibration is at least 3.0x baseline or temperature is at least baseline + 25 C. Temperature is the leading signal for this fault.

title: Overheating and Cooling Fault Guide
text: Overheating and Cooling Fault Guide (MNT-003) - Likely Causes: Failed cooling fan, blocked heat exchanger or filter, stuck thermostat valve, high ambient temperature, or low coolant flow.

title: Overheating and Cooling Fault Guide
text: Overheating and Cooling Fault Guide (MNT-003) - Recommended Actions: Check the cooling fan and airflow, clean the heat exchanger and filters, test the thermostat, and verify coolant flow. If temperature reaches ALARM, reduce load immediately and plan a stop.

title: Overheating and Cooling Fault Guide
text: Overheating and Cooling Fault Guide (MNT-003) - Parts and Downtime: Typical repair takes 12 to 24 hours. Parts: cooling fan assembly, thermostat valve, heat exchanger gasket set.

title: Lubrication Loss Guide
text: Lubrication Loss Guide (MNT-004) - Symptoms and Signals: Lubrication loss raises temperature steadily, with a later rise in vibration. Both signals move together, which separates it from a pure cooling fault.

title: Lubrication Loss Guide
text: Lubrication Loss Guide (MNT-004) - Alert Thresholds: Limits are set per asset from its baseline: ALERT when vibration is at least 2.2x baseline, temperature is at least baseline + 15 C, or motor current is at least 1.25x baseline. ALARM when vibration is at least 3.0x baseline or temperature is at least baseline + 25 C.

title: Lubrication Loss Guide
text: Lubrication Loss Guide (MNT-004) - Likely Causes: Blocked lubrication line, empty reservoir, degraded grease, wrong grease grade, or a missed lubrication schedule.

title: Lubrication Loss Guide
text: Lubrication Loss Guide (MNT-004) - Recommended Actions: Check reservoir level and lines, replace filters, apply the correct grease, and restore the lubrication schedule. Re-check temperature and vibration for two shifts.

title: Lubrication Loss Guide
text: Lubrication Loss Guide (MNT-004) - Parts and Downtime: Typical repair takes 6 to 12 hours. Parts: grease cartridge pack, oil filter, lubrication pump.

title: Motor and Electrical Fault Guide
text: Motor and Electrical Fault Guide (MNT-005) - Symptoms and Signals: Electrical faults show as rising and spiky motor current, a small drop in RPM and a mild temperature rise. Vibration barely changes. A current rise of 25 percent or more over baseline is an ALERT.

title: Motor and Electrical Fault Guide
text: Motor and Electrical Fault Guide (MNT-005) - Alert Thresholds: Limits are set per asset from its baseline: ALERT when vibration is at least 2.2x baseline, temperature is at least baseline + 15 C, or motor current is at least 1.25x baseline. ALARM when vibration is at least 3.0x baseline or temperature is at least baseline + 25 C. For electrical faults motor current is the main signal.

title: Motor and Electrical Fault Guide
text: Motor and Electrical Fault Guide (MNT-005) - Likely Causes: Winding insulation breakdown, pitted contactor contacts, loose terminals, drive board faults, or voltage imbalance.

title: Motor and Electrical Fault Guide
text: Motor and Electrical Fault Guide (MNT-005) - Recommended Actions: Measure insulation resistance, inspect the contactor and terminals, check the drive board, and plan a motor rewind if insulation is poor. Isolate power before any inspection.

title: Motor and Electrical Fault Guide
text: Motor and Electrical Fault Guide (MNT-005) - Parts and Downtime: Typical repair takes 24 to 72 hours. Parts: contactor 40A, motor winding rewind kit, VFD control board.

title: Alert Triage and Escalation
text: Alert Triage and Escalation (SOP-001) - Severity Levels: ALERT means an early warning: schedule an inspection. ALARM means act now: reduce load and plan a stop. A predicted failure with probability of 0.6 or higher within 7 days is treated as an ALERT even if sensors are below their limits.

title: Alert Triage and Escalation
text: Alert Triage and Escalation (SOP-001) - Response Time Limits: ALARM on criticality A assets: acknowledge within 15 minutes and inspect within 2 hours. Criticality B: 1 hour and 8 hours. Criticality C: 4 hours and 48 hours. ALERT on criticality A: acknowledge within 2 hours and inspect by the next planned stop. Criticality B: 8 hours and 3 days. Criticality C: 24 hours and 7 days.

title: Alert Triage and Escalation
text: Alert Triage and Escalation (SOP-001) - Triage Steps: Confirm the signal is real (not a sensor dropout or a short load spike), compare with the last work orders on the asset, check spare part stock, then decide: monitor, inspect, or plan repair. Record the decision and the reason.

title: Alert Triage and Escalation
text: Alert Triage and Escalation (SOP-001) - Human Decision: Predictions are decision aids. A planner or engineer must confirm before a work order is scheduled. Every decision must show the sensor evidence and the rule or manual section behind it.

title: Work Order Creation and Approval
text: Work Order Creation and Approval (SOP-002) - Work Order Types: PREVENTIVE for scheduled routine work (every 30 days per asset). INSPECTION for an alert that needs checking. CORRECTIVE for repair after a failure or a planned repair for a confirmed fault.

title: Work Order Creation and Approval
text: Work Order Creation and Approval (SOP-002) - Approval Limits: Estimated cost below INR 50,000: shift supervisor. INR 50,000 to INR 2,00,000: maintenance manager. Above INR 2,00,000: plant head.

title: Work Order Creation and Approval
text: Work Order Creation and Approval (SOP-002) - Spare Parts Check: Before scheduling, check the part stock at the plant. If stock is zero, raise an emergency purchase (typically 24 to 96 hours) and tell the planner, because it extends downtime.

title: Work Order Creation and Approval
text: Work Order Creation and Approval (SOP-002) - Planning Rule: For criticality A and B assets, plan the repair inside a scheduled stop where possible. Avoid unplanned stops during peak production shifts.

title: OEE Definitions
text: OEE Definitions (REF-001) - Formulas: Availability = run time / planned production time. Performance = (ideal cycle time x total units) / run time. Quality = good units / total units. OEE = Availability x Performance x Quality.

title: OEE Definitions
text: OEE Definitions (REF-001) - Downtime Categories: Breakdown: unplanned stops from failures. Planned maintenance: scheduled preventive work. Small stops: short stops under 30 minutes. Only breakdown and small stops are treated as losses to reduce.

title: OEE Definitions
text: OEE Definitions (REF-001) - Targets: Internal OEE target is 75 percent. A commonly quoted world-class level is 85 percent. Report OEE per asset, line and plant using the same definitions so teams get the same answer.
